chunks: My father (peace be upon him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah al-Barqi narrated to me from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, when the pilgrim prepares his equipment, he does not lift anything nor put it down except that Allah writes for him ten good deeds, erases ten bad deeds, and raises him ten degrees.
And when he mounts his beast, he does not lift a shoe nor put it down except that Allah writes for him the like of that.
And when he performs Tawaf around the House, he goes out from his sins, and when he runs between Safa and Marwa, he goes out from his sins.
So when he stands at Arafat, he goes out from his sins, and when he stands at Masha'ar, he goes out from his sins, and when he throws the pebbles at the Jamarat, he goes out from his sins.
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) enumerated so many and so many stations, all of which expel him from his sins.
Then he said: How can you reach the position of the pilgrim?
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual rewards and sin-expiation associated with the stages of Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-Amal* emphasizes the cumulative spiritual merit of Hajj, distinguishing between the incremental rewards of preparatory actions and the comprehensive expiation of sins achieved through major rituals. It underscores the Shia scholarly view that the physical acts of pilgrimage are not merely obligations but transformative opportunities for spiritual elevation, culminating in a state of purity that distinguishes the pilgrim from the ordinary believer.
